This article analyzes **Indikator 5 baseret på DanStroke**, which tracks the proportion of patients with atrial fibrillation who subsequently develop an ischemic stroke. The data, derived from the DanStroke registry, compares the current measurement period (July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023) against previous years across Danish regions and municipalities [^src1]. The broader Annual Report on Stroke Quality (AFDK) for 2023 and 2024 provides extensive context on these metrics, detailing methodology, national trends, and other clinical indicators across numerous sections [^src2] [^src3] [^src4] [^src5] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8] [^src9] [^src10] [^src11] [^src12] [^src13] [^src14] [^src15] [^src16] [^src17] [^src18] [^src19].

Nationally, [[danmark|Danmark]] shows a positive trend, with the stroke rate among atrial fibrillation patients declining to 0.6% in the current year, down from 0.7% and 0.8% in previous years [^src1]. At the regional level, [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] leads with the lowest rate at 0.3%, followed by [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] at 0.5% and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] at 0.6% [^src1]. Conversely, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] and [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] trail with the highest regional rates, both at 0.8% [^src1].

When examining municipal leaders and trailers, the highest proportions of ischemic stroke are found in smaller municipalities. [[fanoe|Fanø]] records the highest rate at 2.2%, followed by [[dragoer|Dragør]] at 1.7% [^src1]. A group of municipalities, including [[alleroed|Allerød]], [[ballerup|Ballerup]], [[morsoe|Morsø]], and [[norddjurs|Norddjurs]], share a rate of 1.3%, while [[laesoe|Læsø]] sits at 1.2% [^src1]. On the other end of the spectrum, [[lemvig|Lemvig]] is the absolute leader in prevention with a 0.0% rate (0 cases out of 607 patients) [^src1]. Several larger municipalities, including [[kolding|Kolding]], [[middelfart|Middelfart]], [[nyborg|Nyborg]], [[vejen|Vejen]], and [[vejle|Vejle]], achieve a remarkably low rate of 0.1% [^src1].

Trends across the dated sections reveal a general national improvement, though local performance varies. For example, [[frederiksvaerk-hundested|Frederiksværk-Hundested]] saw its rate drop significantly from 1.2% in previous years to 0.4% in the current period [^src1]. However, statistical outliers are heavily influenced by population size; municipalities with suppressed patient counts (marked with `#` to preserve anonymity) often exhibit extreme percentages and wide confidence intervals, such as Fanø (0.5–6.3) and Læsø (0.0–6.4), making their high rates less statistically stable than the consistent low performers like Lemvig and Kolding [^src1]. No explicit target threshold is defined in the dataset, making year-over-year reduction the primary measure of success.
